Differential expression: one comparison

Source: vignettes/articles/de-single.Rmd
de-single.Rmd

Question: which genes change between two conditions, by how much, and how does that depend on their expression level?

Function Use
standardize_de() read any DE table into standard columns (used by every DE plot)
plot_volcano() fold change against significance
plot_ma() fold change against mean expression
filter_de_genes() up- and down-regulated genes as two tables
rank_de_genes(), generate_de_rank_file() genes ranked by signed significance, for GSEA

Data: macrophages of 6 donors, naive or stimulated with interferon-γ (IFN-γ) (Alasoo et al. 2018). The same comparison is tested with edgeR and with DESeq2, paired by donor (design ~ donor + condition), to show that the plots read either.

mac <- docs_macrophage()
keep <- mac$samples$condition %in% c("naive", "IFNg")
counts <- filter_low_expression_genes(mac$counts[, keep], min_group_size = 6)
samples <- droplevels(mac$samples[keep, ])

# edgeR quasi-likelihood test
design <- model.matrix(~ donor + condition, data = samples)
y <- edgeR::normLibSizes(edgeR::DGEList(counts))
fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(y, design)
test <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionIFNg")
de_edger <- edgeR::topTags(test, n = Inf)

# DESeq2 Wald test, with shrunken fold changes
dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    counts,
    samples,
    design = ~ donor + condition
)
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
de_deseq <- DESeq2::results(dds, name = "condition_IFNg_vs_naive")
shrunk <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(
    dds,
    coef = "condition_IFNg_vs_naive",
    type = "normal",
    quiet = TRUE
)
de_deseq$log2FoldChange_shrunk <- shrunk$log2FoldChange

Fold-change shrinkage pulls the noisy fold changes of lowly expressed genes towards 0. type = "normal" is built into DESeq2; its authors recommend type = "apeglm" (package apeglm) or "ashr" when installed.

Reading DE tables

Every DE plot of the package reads its input with standardize_de(), which recognises edgeR, DESeq2, limma and Seurat tables from their column names and returns standard columns (feature, logfc, pvalue, padj, mean_expr, then the table’s other columns):

head(standardize_de(de_edger), 3)
#> Detected edgeR results (logFC, PValue, FDR)
#>     feature     logfc       pvalue         padj mean_expr         F
#> 1 LINC01645 -6.445168 6.906463e-11 8.637223e-07 0.6412643  385.2972
#> 2     TAGAP  3.291148 2.793358e-10 1.119023e-06 7.3802895 1844.1143
#> 3      NOD2  3.386661 2.828302e-10 1.119023e-06 5.6846857 1838.0587
head(standardize_de(de_deseq, logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk"), 3)
#> Detected DESeq2 results (log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj)
#> 4 p-values of 0 replaced by 2.55999999769412e-315 (a tenth of the smallest non-zero value)
#> 4 adjusted p-values of 0 replaced by 6.41000000000069e-312 (a tenth of the smallest non-zero value)
#>   feature      logfc       pvalue         padj mean_expr log2FoldChange
#> 1    SPP1 -0.6664640 1.908393e-03 4.255770e-03  556815.1     -0.6902862
#> 2    ACTB  0.6581395 1.336112e-12 1.175064e-11  574651.6      0.6628589
#> 3     FTL  0.1154071 3.866035e-01 4.721085e-01  404628.0      0.1122727
#>        lfcSE       stat
#> 1 0.22237667 -3.1041303
#> 2 0.09348526  7.0905178
#> 3 0.12967607  0.8657933
method log fold change p-value adjusted p mean expression
edgeR logFC PValue FDR logCPM (log2)
DESeq2 log2FoldChange pvalue padj baseMean (linear)
limma logFC P.Value adj.P.Val AveExpr (log2)
Seurat avg_log2FC p_val p_val_adj none

Any other table works with the columns given explicitly (logfc.col, p.col, padj.col, mean.col, feature.col); the same arguments are accepted by every DE plot. p-values of exactly 0 (underflow) are replaced by a tenth of the smallest non-zero value, and NA p-values (DESeq2’s independent filtering) are treated as not significant.

Volcano plot 

plot_volcano(de_edger, label.n = 6)

The y-axis is the −log10 adjusted p-value, the value that decides significance, so the dashed line is the padj.cutoff. The label.n most significant genes of each direction are labelled (10 by default), among them interferon-γ targets such as IRF1, APOL4 and UBD.

Variants

A minimum absolute fold change for significance, drawn as dashed lines:

plot_volcano(de_edger, logfc.cutoff = 2, label.n = 5)

label = "selected" labels only the genes given, significant or not; label = "top" with label.features adds them to the top genes:

plot_volcano(
    de_edger,
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("STAT1", "IRF1", "CIITA", "HLA-DRA", "ACTB")
)

The top genes ranked by "padj" (default), "logfc" or "product" of both:

plot_volcano(de_edger, label.rank = "product", label.n = 6)

"arrow" names the directions with arrows and counts at the top (and drops the legend); "none" hides the counts:

plot_volcano(
    de_edger,
    annotate.counts = "arrow",
    up.label = "Up in IFN-γ",
    down.label = "Down in IFN-γ",
    label.n = 5
)

Colours named up, down, ns (any of them):

plot_volcano(
    de_deseq,
    logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk",
    label = "none",
    cols = c(up = "#B5338A", down = "#2C5DA8")
)

MA plot

Fold change against mean expression shows how both depend on the expression level. edgeR’s logCPM is already log2 and drawn as it is:

plot_ma(de_edger, label.n = 5)

Variants

DESeq2’s baseMean is linear and drawn on a log10 axis (mean.scale is taken from the method). With shrunken fold changes, the lowly expressed genes on the left no longer fan out:

plot_ma(
    de_deseq,
    logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk",
    label.n = 5
)

The same genes without shrinkage, for comparison:

plot_ma(de_deseq, label = "none")

A robust trend line (lowess) through all genes: a trend away from 0 would point to an expression-dependent bias, such as a normalization problem.

plot_ma(de_edger, trend = TRUE, label = "none")

Gene lists

filter_de_genes() splits a DE table into up- and down-regulated genes (the rows of the table, with all its columns), by adjusted p-value and absolute fold change:

de_lists <- filter_de_genes(
    as.data.frame(de_edger),
    padj.cutoff = 0.05,
    logfc.cutoff = 1
)
#> Detected edgeR results (logFC, FDR)
vapply(de_lists, nrow, integer(1))
#>   up_reg down_reg 
#>     1061      936
head(rownames(de_lists$up_reg))
#> [1] "TAGAP" "NOD2"  "UBD"   "LRRK2" "IRF1"  "APOL4"

rank_de_genes() ranks all genes by the signed significance −log10(adjusted p) × sign(log fold change), the “pi-value”: strongly up-regulated genes first, strongly down-regulated last. generate_de_rank_file() returns (and with file, writes) the two-column .rnk table of the GSEA desktop application:

ranked <- rank_de_genes(as.data.frame(de_edger))
head(ranked[c("logFC", "FDR", "piValue", "rank")], 3)
#>           logFC          FDR  piValue rank
#> TAGAP  3.291148 1.119023e-06 5.951161    1
#> NOD2   3.386661 1.119023e-06 5.951161    2
#> UBD   10.178219 1.119023e-06 5.951161    3
# file = "ifng.rnk" writes it
rnk <- generate_de_rank_file(as.data.frame(de_edger))
head(rnk, 3)
#>   GeneName     rank
#> 1    TAGAP 5.951161
#> 2     NOD2 5.951161
#> 3      UBD 5.951161

For fgsea or clusterProfiler, the ranking is a named vector: setNames(rnk$rank, rnk$GeneName) (see Gene-set enrichment). Many genes share the largest −log10 adjusted p-values; ranking by the test statistic (edgeR F with the fold change sign, DESeq2 stat) breaks such ties and is a common alternative.

These three functions take the same method, logfc.col and padj.col as the plots (renamed in 0.10.0 from de_method, log2fc_col, pvalue_col; the old names still work, with a deprecation warning).
